top_issues.issue: Rock reads as flat square tiles, not cubic faceted stone
top_issues.why: 03 shows chunky blocks with varied facets, bevels and offset depth; here every cell is the same smooth square front with a seam, so mass looks like wallpaper.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Per-block depth jitter, chamfered/bevelled edges, and a few low-poly facet planes per front so lamp light catches different angles.

top_issues.issue: Fissures are decals that don't light surrounding stone
top_issues.why: 04's defining trait is fissures washing the rock around them; here glow is a soft per-tile square and veins end at tile edges.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Continue veins across neighbouring tiles and add a falloff emissive/light pool onto adjacent faces, keeping the far mass dark.

top_issues.issue: No world-specific material character in the rock
top_issues.why: CRYOS and MAELIS differ only by tint; 05 wants crystalline sheen catching the lamp and 06 wants nacre iridescence.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Per-world material response: sharp specular/fresnel on CRYOS faces, subtle hue-shifting sheen on MAELIS faces under the lamp.

top_issues.issue: Unlit rock collapses to a flat dark grid
top_issues.why: Darkness should be real but faces should still separate by a hair of value near light; the visible grid seams read as UI not stone.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Soften seam lines in unlit areas and let block silhouettes, not grid lines, carry form; keep true black for void.

top_issues.issue: Mid-depth rock loses its world hue

top_issues.issue: MAELIS core chamber drifts to violet and grey

top_issues.issue: MAELIS lacks nacre and iridescence and reads as a green CRYOS

top_issues.issue: Ore and pickup colours are shared across worlds

top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep ore readable, but tint its glow halo toward the world palette, or make the dominant ore per world sit closer to the world hue.

top_issues.issue: Gravity-zone chevrons and rain overload the frame

top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the tint and edge frame, but thin the chevron density and opacity outside the player's vicinity and reduce the rain streak count; keep the cyan zones as they are.

top_issues.suggested_direction: Give ledges more chunky block depth and visible cut-stone faces lit from the nearest sconce.

top_issues.why: The amber-on-cool masonry contrast at the heart of the art direction is missing in most rooms.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add sconces near key platforms with a larger warm wash on the adjacent stone.

top_issues.issue: Footing gets lost in dark vaults
top_issues.why: Dark decks on a dark void rely on thin cracks; enemies blend in.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a consistent lit lip on walkable tops; rim the enemies.

top_issues.issue: Gravity-zone chevrons and rain overload the frame
top_issues.why: Dense overlays compete with the hazards and the stone.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Thin the chevron density and the rain; keep the tint and frame.

top_issues.issue: Platforms read as thin slabs rather than dressed stone
top_issues.why: They lack the chunky cut-masonry mass of the references.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give ledges thicker block depth with lit cut faces.

Warm amber-on-black panel with bracket corners, lit ore icons and clear totals; the most on-tone screen, and the debt line in red reads well.
Quiet dark vignette with a softly glowing title suits 'sacred and quiet'; the body is a dense centered italic block that is a bit grey and long-lined.

top_issues.issue: HUD bars and captions are thin and low-contrast
top_issues.why: FUEL/HULL labels and the LUMENS/CARGO captions are tiny and wash out on the bright sky or disappear on dark rock; at a glance readability suffers.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Put a subtle dark backing plate or soft drop shadow behind the corner clusters and lift the caption size and weight slightly. Keep it minimal.

top_issues.issue: Title CTA stack reads like a website
top_issues.why: The boxed advance line, 'Wishlist on Steam' link and keybind footer feel like web chrome under a strong cinematic wordmark, which dilutes the descent mood of reference 01.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Fold the advance text into the DESCEND button area or drop it in weight, and let more black plus the warm glow rising from below carry the lower half.

top_issues.issue: Cargo readout is small and floats
top_issues.why: The ore list at bottom right is unanchored and hard to read over rock.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Group it under the 7/10 counter on a faint panel and use slightly larger icons.

top_issues.issue: Ending text block is dense
top_issues.why: Six centered italic lines in mid-grey are tiring to read and lack the ceremony the glowing title sets up.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use shorter line lengths, paragraph breaks and slightly warmer, brighter text. Consider a staged reveal.

Leaf or teardrop shape is softer than the crisp octahedron or brilliant on the sheet; no sparkle or caustics.
Small black shards inside an orange square; at gameplay size it reads as a copper/gold-ish warm tile, not a black shard with sparks.
Black shards with glowing seams and sparks are right, but the shards are small and the uniform orange glow is closer to the copper halo than to 'angry'.
Unmistakable teal; the only plant.
Fronds are thin and pale; the glow floods the tile into a flat teal square cut off at the tile edge.
Red halo against the violet gem clearly flags the trap.
Husk plus gem plus crack lines read, but the cracks are pale orange rather than red and the white husk is brighter than a rock shell.
Round lavender starburst reads instantly on the blue rock.
Radial frost flower with a soft cold glow; on-brief.
Translucent blue cubes with a cyan glow; distinct from frostbloom.
Cube shape and glacier blue are right; frosted top and internal fractures are missing.

top_issues.issue: Glow is a flat square clipped to the tile
top_issues.why: The halo fills the cell edge-to-edge and stops hard at the tile boundary, so ore reads as coloured tiles rather than light blooming into the dark and washing the neighbouring rock.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use a radial falloff centred on the mineral that fades before the tile edge and lets a little light spill onto adjacent faces; keep the brightest light at the base.

top_issues.issue: Iron vanishes against host rock
top_issues.why: With no glow and small dark forms, iron is the hardest ore to spot at gameplay size; the brief says it must separate by gunmetal-blue colour, crisp cubic facets and specular.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make the cubes larger and chunkier, push the gunmetal-blue value up on the lit faces, and add stronger specular edges or blue glints; drop the L-shaped slab silhouettes.

top_issues.issue: Nacre silhouette does not match the shell brief
top_issues.why: A spiky crystal cluster reads as another gem and blurs nacre with frostbloom, silver and diamond among the pale ores.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build a scalloped fan or shell with stepped ribbed layers and a pearly sheen rather than a hard halo.

top_issues.issue: Embershard reads as a warm tile, not a black shard
top_issues.why: The shard is small inside a strong orange glow, so at distance it falls into the gold/copper warm family instead of 'black shard peppered with sparks'.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Enlarge the obsidian slabs to dominate the tile, shrink the ambient glow, and push the light into the seams and pinpoint sparks.

top_issues.issue: Silver needles are detached and faint
top_issues.why: Floating blades with no root break the 'fan erupting from rock' read, and the pale halo muddies the distinction from frostbloom and diamond.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Root the needles in a shared base and fan them upward densely; rely on bright metallic edges instead of a halo.
